name: osmotic_growth_division
description: A reusable osmotic growth-and-division module (metabolism → growth & division). An internal autocatalytic osmolyte source coupled to compartment osmotic physics: product accumulation → osmotic pressure (van 't Hoff) → solvent influx → volume growth → division at a size threshold. Membrane permeability sets the fate: too permeable starves (product leaks, no osmotic build-up), too impermeable lyses (pressure bursts the membrane), matched gives sustained growth → division. Units-typed, mass-conserving coarse-grained reproduction (not wrapped membrane MD).

network_throughput.description: Internal autocatalytic/metabolic osmolyte source rate (mole/second); ~0 = ablation control

membrane_permeability.description: Membrane solute permeability (meter/second); the fate knob (leaky→starve, tight→lyse)

division_threshold.description: Volume at which the compartment divides (liter); default 1.6× initial volume

leak_rate.description: Multiplier on the solute permeability for the outward leak (dimensionless)

cell_process.doc:
Couples an internal autocatalytic osmolyte source to compartment osmotic
physics: product accumulation → osmotic pressure → solvent influx → volume
growth → division at a size threshold (or lysis if the pressure bursts the
membrane, or starvation if the product leaks away before it can build). A
coarse-grained, units-typed, mass-conserving reproduction — not wrapped MD.

Stateful: the compartment's volume ``V`` and internal osmolyte amount ``N``
are integrated across calls (like a genuine ODE integrator), sub-stepped for
stability. Each ``update`` advances one ``interval`` and emits the volume,
internal concentration, osmotic pressure, product amount, division count /
event, lysis flag, net growth, the mass-balance residual, and an outcome code
(0 starve · 1 grow-no-division · 2 divide · 3 lysis).

_contract.summary: Internal autocatalytic osmolyte source coupled to compartment osmotic physics: product → osmotic pressure → solvent influx → volume growth → division (or lysis / starvation set by membrane permeability).
_contract.description: Coarse-grained, units-typed, mass-conserving reproduction of metabolism changing a protocell's physical fate. An internal autocatalytic/metabolic source (reduced rTCA-style turn) makes an osmolyte; its accumulation sets the internal concentration and, by van 't Hoff, the osmotic pressure; that pressure drives solvent influx across a semi-permeable membrane and the compartment expands; at a volume threshold it divides (V and N halved, mass conserved). The membrane permeability lets solutes and solvent cross and decides the fate: too permeable starves (product leaks, no osmotic build-up), too impermeable lyses (pressure spikes past the burst tension), matched gives sustained growth → division. Not a wrapped membrane-MD engine.

inputs.external_osmolyte: external osmolyte concentration c_out (molar); the leak/osmosis reference, default 0

outputs.osmotic_pressure: van 't Hoff osmotic pressure Pi = R T (c_in - c_out) (pascal)
outputs.product_amount: internal osmolyte amount N in this lineage (mole)
outputs.division_event: 1 on an interval in which a division occurred, else 0 (integer)
outputs.lysed: 1 once the osmotic pressure has burst the membrane, else 0 (integer)
outputs.net_growth: V / V0 — net volume growth factor (dimensionless)
outputs.osmolyte_balance_residual: (N0 + produced) - (N + leaked + daughter_mass) — the growth/division mass-conservation witness (~0) (mole)
outputs.outcome_code: physical fate: 0 starve · 1 grow-no-division · 2 divide · 3 lysis (integer)

math: c_in = N/V ; Pi = R T (c_in - c_out)
V >= division_threshold => V,N := V/2, N/2 (divide) ; Pi >= lysis_pressure => lyse
assumptions: Coarse-grained reproduction; the proposed primary method is custom membrane kinetics (full membrane MD is out of environment).
van 't Hoff ideal-dilute osmotic pressure Pi = R T (c_in - c_out).
Spherical compartment: A = (36 pi)^(1/3) V^(2/3); solvent influx dV/dt = Lp A Pi.
membrane_permeability is the solute permeability P_s (m/s); solvent hydraulic conductivity Lp is finite and fixed, so osmotic pressure can build (lysis) when influx + division cannot relieve it.
Division halves V and N (mass conserved); lysis when Pi >= lysis_pressure; starvation when the compartment never grows.

emitter.doc:
Store historical states in memory.

``subsample`` records only every Nth composite tick (default 1 =
every tick). Use this for long runs or composites with heavy
state (large fields, many agents) to keep RAM bounded — the
saved time-series still reflects the simulation's true cadence
via each row's ``global_time`` field.

``max_len`` optionally bounds ``history`` to the most recent N
recorded rows (a ring buffer): once the cap is reached each new
record drops the oldest. Default ``None`` = unbounded (the
historical behaviour — consumers such as v2ecoli that read the
full ``history`` are unaffected unless they opt in). ``max_len``
counts *recorded* rows (i.e. post-``subsample``).
